1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application is disposed of.

3. The present petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No.640/2018 under Sections 406/498A/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) registered at Police Station Khajuri Khas, Delhi on the ground of settlement.
4. The petitioner no.1 is the husband of the respondent no.2 and the This is a digitally signed order.

The marriage of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 was solemnized on 6th February, 2013 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
One child was born out of the wedlock, who is still a minor.

sentences.text: Disputes arose between the parties and their respective families, which resulted in filing of the FIR by the respondent no.2 against the petitioners.

6. Subsequently, the parties have settled their disputes before the Counsellor, Family Court,
Shahdara District in terms of Settlement Agreement dated 11th October, 2023, which has been filed as Annexure-B to the petition.
The parties have also been granted divorce by mutual consent.

7. As per the settlement, entire amount of Rs.4,50,000/- has been paid by the petitioners to the respondent no.2.
8.
Issue notice.

9. Notice is accepted by the learned APP appearing on behalf of the State and by the counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent no. 2.
10.
The respondent no.2 is present in Court and has been identified by her counsel and by the Investigating Officer (IO).
She informs the Court that she has settled the matter of her own free will and without any coercion.
She further states that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.
11. The petitioners are also present in Court and have been identified by their counsel.
They affirm the statement of the respondent no.2 and undertake to abide by the terms of settlement arrived at between the parties.

12. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 14/12/2023 at 02:03:31 the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the aforementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
13. There is one minor child born from the wedlock, who is in the care and custody of the respondent no.2/mother.
It is directed that the settlement executed between the petitioners and respondent no.2 as well as this order shall have no effect on the rights of the minor child/children in the future.
14. Consequently, FIR No.640/2018 registered at Police Station Khajuri Khas and proceedings pursuant thereto are quashed.
15. The petition stands disposed of.

AMIT BANSAL, J.
